ACCEPTThe connected-residual amplification theorem is correct as stated. The arbitrary-exterior cap applies to the linked modules, the zero-cost implication gives the required path-domination bound, and the proposed final forming set is inclusion-minimal for every  $s\ge1$ . Thus
$$\boxed{\operatorname{SF}_2(J_s)=12s+2,\qquad
\operatorname{SF}_2(R_s)\le 12s-\left\lceil\frac{s}{3}\right\rceil}$$
and consequently
$$\boxed{\operatorname{SF}_2(J_s)-
\bigl(2+\operatorname{SF}_2(R_s)\bigr)
\ge \left\lceil\frac{s}{3}\right\rceil.}$$
I extracted and ran the unchanged new checker with assertions enabled. It exited successfully, and both its regenerated report file and its stdout match the supplied report byte for byte.My review concerns the four embedded files in    connected-residual-review-package.txt. There is one attachment-completeness issue: the full square-ear lemma is referenced rather than supplied. I reconstruct the needed lemma below, so this leaves no unresolved mathematical dependency in this verdict.1. Formation semantics and the arbitrary-exterior capFor a graph  $H$  and selected set  $S$ , write
$$\operatorname{Act}_H(S)
=\{v\in S:N_H(v)\cap S\ne\varnothing\}.$$
The stated non-induced  $K_{1,2}$  convention says that  $S$  forms  $H$  precisely when every  $x\notin S$  satisfies
$$|N_H(x)\cap S|\ge2
\quad\text{or}\quad
N_H(x)\cap\operatorname{Act}_H(S)\ne\varnothing.
\tag{2}$$
Here  $\operatorname{SF}_2(H)$  is the maximum cardinality of an inclusion-minimal forming set.Formation is upward closed: enlarging  $S$  cannot reduce the number of selected neighbours or deactivate a selected vertex. Consequently, testing every single deletion suffices for inclusion-minimality. These tests must include the newly deleted vertex and recompute activity; the paper’s witness arguments and the checker both do this correctly.Why the cap remains valid after connecting the modulesFix one ten-vertex block in module  $j$ . Its only edges to vertices outside that block are the two edges from its  $Z$  vertices to  $y_j$ . The other block, the path neighbours of  $y_j$ , and—in  $J_s$ —the root adjacent to  $y_j$ , all belong to the exterior at the same interface.The supplying proof’s safe deletions avoid  $Z$  and  $y_j$ . The relevant preservation argument is:If  $y_j$  is selected, its selected neighbours are unchanged by such a deletion. Its activity is therefore unchanged. This preserves every exterior formation condition that uses  $y_j$ .If  $y_j$  is outside, the supplier’s cases preserve its formation by retaining an active selected  $Z$ , retaining two selected  $Z$  neighbours, or, when no  $Z$  was selected in this block, leaving the exterior contribution unchanged.Every other exterior vertex has no direct edge to the deleted block vertex. Its selected-neighbour information and the relevant activities therefore remain unchanged.This is the reason the local contradictions remain contradictions to global inclusion-minimality. No restriction of  $S$  to a block or to an  $F_2$  module is assumed to be minimal by itself.I also checked the supplying case split:  $w,z>0$ ;  $w=0,z>0$ ;  $z=0$ ; and the sharper  $y\in S,z=0$  case. The deletion choices retain the interface properties just described. The added path edges create no new way for one of those deletions to fail outside the block.Let  $b_{j,1}$  and  $b_{j,2}$  be the selected counts in the two blocks of module  $j$ . The supplying inequalities give
$$b_{j,k}\le6,\qquad
Z_{j,k}\cap S\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow b_{j,k}\le5,\qquad
y_j\in S\Longrightarrow b_{j,k}\le5.$$
Thus the full module contribution
$$m_j=\mathbf 1_{\{y_j\in S\}}+b_{j,1}+b_{j,2}$$
satisfies:Condition in module  $j$ Bound $y_j\notin S$  $m_j\le12$  $y_j\in S$  $m_j\le1+5+5=11$  $y_j\notin S$ , with some local  $Z$  selected $m_j\le5+6=11$ These are exactly the three bounds required by the new construction.2. Construction, connectivity and bipartitenessEach  $F_2$  module contains two ten-vertex blocks and its common vertex  $y_j$ , hence has 21 vertices. Connecting successive  $y_j$ ’s gives
$$|V(R_s)|=21s.$$
Every module is connected, and the added edges connect their  $y_j$ ’s in a path, so  $R_s$  is connected.The stated local bipartition is valid. Reversing it on even-indexed modules places successive  $y_j$ ’s on opposite sides. Therefore every added path edge crosses the global bipartition.Putting  $d$  on the right and  $e$  on the left makes the following edges cross that same partition: $dy_j$  for odd  $j$ ; $ey_j$  for even  $j$ ; $de$ .The base is connected even at  $s=1$ :  $d$  meets  $y_1$ , and  $e$  meets  $d$ . Adding  $\alpha$  on the left and  $\beta$  on the right completes the square without violating bipartiteness or connectivity. Hence
$$|V(J_s)|=21s+4,
\qquad B_s-\{d,e\}=R_s.$$
The degree assertions also hold. Each residual  $y_j$  has four block neighbours and at most two path neighbours; every other residual vertex has degree at most five. Thus
$$\Delta(R_s)\le6.$$
In the final graph,
$$\deg(d)=\left\lceil\frac{s}{2}\right\rceil+2,
\qquad
\deg(e)=\left\lfloor\frac{s}{2}\right\rfloor+2.$$
Their growth is consistent with the stated scope: there is no uniform final-degree claim.3. The residual upper bound: zero cost really forces dominationLet  $S$  be any globally inclusion-minimal forming set of  $R_s$ . The modules partition its vertex set, so define
$$S_j=S\cap V(F_{2,j}),\qquad
c_j=12-|S_j|.$$
The module cap proves
$$c_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.$$
Suppose  $c_j=0$ . Then  $|S_j|=12$ . Both sharper bounds must be avoided, giving
$$y_j\notin S,
\qquad
S\cap Z_{j,1}=S\cap Z_{j,2}=\varnothing.
\tag{3}$$
All four local  $Z$  vertices are therefore omitted.In the residual graph, the complete neighbourhood of  $y_j$  consists of these four  $Z$  vertices and its existing path neighbours. By (3), the only possible selected neighbours of this outside vertex are
$$y_{j-1},\quad y_{j+1},$$
with nonexistent endpoints omitted.Every vertex satisfying the formation condition (2) has at least one selected neighbour. Consequently, some existing path neighbour  $y_i$  must be selected. The selected- $y_i$  cap then gives
$$|S_i|\le11,\qquad c_i\ge1.
\tag{4}$$
The distinction between necessity and sufficiency is handled correctly here. If  $y_j$  has only one selected path neighbour, that neighbour must additionally be active for formation. The proof uses only the weaker necessary statement that a selected path neighbour exists. Dropping the activity requirement at this step weakens the obstruction and still yields a valid upper bound.Now put
$$D=\{j:c_j\ge1\}.$$
Every index outside  $D$  has zero cost and, by (4), has a path neighbour in  $D$ . Every index in  $D$  belongs to its own closed neighbourhood. Therefore  $D$  is a closed dominating set of  $P_s$ :
$$\{1,\ldots,s\}
=\bigcup_{j\in D}N_{P_s}[j].$$
Since each such neighbourhood contains at most three indices,
$$s
\le\sum_{j\in D}|N_{P_s}[j]|
\le3|D|.$$
Finally,
$$\sum_{j=1}^s c_j
\ge |D|
\ge\left\lceil\frac{s}{3}\right\rceil,$$
and hence
$$|S|
=\sum_{j=1}^s(12-c_j)
\le12s-\left\lceil\frac{s}{3}\right\rceil.$$
Taking the maximum over globally minimal forming sets proves the asserted residual upper bound.There is no missing endpoint case. At  $s=1$ , zero cost would leave  $y_1$  with no selected neighbour, so the sole module must have positive cost. At  $s=2$ , and at the endpoints of longer paths, the closed-neighbourhood count remains valid; their neighbourhoods simply have fewer than three vertices.The proof never claims that domination is sufficient to construct a residual forming set. It therefore does not establish, or inadvertently assume, an exact residual value for general  $s$ .4. The square-ear lemma, reconstructed directlyThe package refers to a separate square-ear note, but its full proof is absent. The precise lemma needed here has the following complete proof.Lemma. Suppose  $d\alpha\beta ed$  is a square, with  $\alpha,\beta$  having no exterior neighbours and  $d,e$  allowed arbitrary exterior neighbours. Every globally inclusion-minimal forming set selects exactly two square vertices.Proof.First, a forming set cannot select fewer than two:With no square vertex selected,  $\alpha$  has no selected neighbour.If only  $d$  is selected,  $\beta$  has no selected neighbour. The case of only  $e$  is symmetric.If only  $\alpha$  is selected,  $\beta$ ’s sole selected neighbour is  $\alpha$ , which is inactive because both its neighbours  $d,\beta$  are omitted. The case of only  $\beta$  is symmetric.Now suppose at least three square vertices are selected.If both roots  $d,e$  are selected, delete a selected interior vertex. The roots remain active through  $de$ ; every outside interior vertex is formed through its adjacent active root. Exterior formation is preserved because only the roots have exterior neighbours and both remain selected and active.If only  $d$  is selected among the roots, the square selection must be
$$\{d,\alpha,\beta\}.$$
Delete  $\beta$ . The retained pair  $d,\alpha$  is active; it forms newly outside  $\beta$  through  $\alpha$  and outside  $e$  through  $d$ . Exterior formation is again preserved. The case with only  $e$  selected is symmetric.Each case with at least three selections admits a safe deletion, contradicting minimality. Thus exactly two are selected.  $\square$ This proof covers arbitrary exterior root degrees and supplies the exact lemma used by the new theorem.5. Exact final value and all attainment witnessesUpper boundFor any globally minimal forming set of  $J_s$ , the square lemma contributes exactly two selections, and each of the  $s$  modules contributes at most twelve. These sets of vertices partition  $V(J_s)$ . Therefore
$$\operatorname{SF}_2(J_s)\le12s+2.$$
AttainmentIn every block select
$$T=A\cup V\cup\{p,u\},$$
and select both roots  $d,e$ . Omit all  $y_j$ , all  $W,Z$ , and  $\alpha,\beta$ . Call the resulting set  $S^\ast$ . Its size is
$$|S^\ast|=2s\cdot6+2=12s+2.$$
It forms the entire graph:Every outside  $w_i$  has selected neighbours  $v_i,u$ .Every outside  $z_i$  has selected neighbours  $a_i,p$ .The roots are mutually active through  $de$ .Every  $y_j$  has its designated active root neighbour. $\alpha$  has active neighbour  $d$ , and  $\beta$  has active neighbour  $e$ .All single-deletion witnesses are valid:Deleted vertexFailure after deletion $a_i$  $z_i$  has only selected neighbour  $p$ ;  $p$  is inactive because all  $Z$  remain omitted. $v_i$  $w_i$  has only selected neighbour  $u$ ;  $u$  is inactive because all  $W$  remain omitted. $p$ The newly outside  $p$  has no selected neighbour. $u$ The newly outside  $u$  has no selected neighbour. $d$  $\alpha$  has no selected neighbour: its neighbours are  $d,\beta$ , both now omitted. $e$  $\beta$  has no selected neighbour: its neighbours are  $\alpha,e$ , both now omitted.The path and root edges cannot repair a block witness. They attach through  $y_j$ , which remains omitted in every block-deletion test, and they add no neighbours to  $p,u,w_i,z_i$  beyond those already accounted for.Every single deletion therefore fails. Upward closure proves that  $S^\ast$  is inclusion-minimal, yielding
$$\operatorname{SF}_2(J_s)\ge12s+2.$$
Together with the upper bound, this proves the exact final value for every  $s\ge1$ .At  $s=1$ , the residual is the original  $F_2$ , with exact value eleven, and the final value is fourteen. This boundary case agrees with the general discrepancy bound.6.
